- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the middle of the forecast (e.g., 10–20 days), suggesting it underweights recent downward momentum or fails to adjust to mean-reverting trends.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values show downward correction or consolidation.
- Model often fails to capture short-term volatility clustering — underestimates sharp drops or overestimates slow recoveries.
- When history shows strong downward trend, model still projects upward bias — suggests it doesn’t sufficiently weight recent low values.
- Model is sensitive to recent high values — overweights recent peaks and underweights recent troughs in its smoothing mechanism.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently biased upward, especially in the first 10 days, then gradually corrects but often lags behind true mean reversion.
